newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First popularity slips since election.
newsitem.headline: NZ First popularity slips since election.

text.p: New Zealand First's popularity has declined since the general election according to an opinion poll taken after it chose National as its coalition partner, TVNZ said on Thursday.
The Colmar Brunton poll showed National up one point from election night to 35 percent, and Labour unchanged on 28 percent.
NZ First slipped to eight percent from 13 percent on election night, the Alliance fell to seven percent from 10 percent, and Act support declined to 4.5 percent from six percent.
Of NZ First voters in the election, 63 percent remained loyal, 18 percent said they would now vote for Labour, 5.5 percent would switch to National and 13 percent didn't know.
TVNZ said 49 percent of respondents agreed with NZ First's decision to choose National, 38 percent disagreed and 13 percent didn't know. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
